4.text: Leo is called Vêˊtča-ñeˊut (“standing-woman”). This name is usually
4.note: two stress marks, one after ê and one after e in ñe'ut, both raised comma shape, confirmed at 2x.

5.text: given to women taking part in certain ceremonial dances.¹ The woman
5.note: footnote marker is the printed superscript 1 (U+00B9), tight against the period per §2.10; the machine draft showed a bare '!' but the raster is unambiguous.

6.text: is considered to be Orion’s wife, and she sleeps on the bare ground. In a

7.text: quarrel she struck Orion on the back with her tailoring-board, causing his

8.text: back to become crooked. After that he drove his wife out, and she lay

9.text: down to sleep in the middle of the sky. Leo is formed of seven stars. The

10.text: star ε of Leo represents the head of the woman; η, her neck; Regulus, her
10.note: ε and η are Greek Bayer star letters (apparatus, not Tier-1 notation), keyed plain.

11.text: knee. A small star between ε and η represents the sleeve on which rests

12.text: the head of the sleeping woman. Other stars outline her body.

13.text: The Pleiades are called Ñaus˙qaǰoˊmkɪn (“group of women”). They
13.note: dot after 's' sits mid-height, keyed as the palatalization mark U+02D9 per §2.1/§2.6 (s is a licensed base); the raised caron over j gives ǰ (English 'joy') per §2.2; middle-dot U+00B7 is the listed lookalike trap for this mark (§3).

14.text: are six young women waiting for husbands. Orion, after his quarrel with

15.text: his wife, offered to marry one of them; but they rejected his offer,

16.text: considering his membrum virile to be too big for them. The incensed suitor

17.text: caught up his bow and began to shoot at the women, who turned and fled.

18.text: Aldebaran is considered to be the copper-tipped arrow of Orion, and is

19.text: called ČêˊLo-maˊᵋqim (“copper arrow”). The rear end of its wooden shaft is
19.note: the compound mark after ma' is stress U+02CA then laryngeal U+1D4B stacked on the same vowel, per the two-superscript-marks pattern (stress first, then the open-curl laryngeal) — not an uncatalogued 's'-shaped glyph. The medial capital L in 'Lo' is a genuine full cap, matching the height of the word-initial Č, confirmed at 4x and corroborated by the machine draft which also read a capital L; flagging as an unresolved medial-capital doubt for adjudication rather than silently lowering it.

20.text: represented by the double star not far from Aldebaran. The arrow fell short

21.text: of the fleeing women, and stuck in a mossy bog. The bow of Orion is

22.text: represented by a number of stars in front of the constellation, which form a

23.text: figure somewhat resembling a bow. The Kolyma Chukchee say that the

24.text: “group of women” stand quiet, and protect themselves with nets, which

25.text: are represented by a number of small stars. The “copper arrow” sticks in

27.text: The three constellations described by the Chukchee are shown in Fig.

28.text: 214. Orion is standing with shoulders squared and legs wide apart, and is

29.text: bending his bow for another shot.

30.text: The star α (Capella) of the Wagoner is a reindeer-buck which is tied

31.text: behind the sledge of a man (ε) who is driving two reindeer. All four stars

32.text: are called čŭmña-nleteˊtɪlɪn (“buck-carriers”). β of the same constellation is
32.note: breve over u (ŭ) confirmed at 2x per §2.2/§2.6; both i-forms in the suffix are dotless ɪ, contrasted against dotted 'i' in neighbouring English words on the same sheet.

33.text: supposed to be a scarf lost by another reindeer-driver, who now comes back

34.text: for it. This driver has behind his sledge another extra buck (star θ), which

35.text: is walking sidewise. A fox is approaching the scarf from the other side.

36.text: The whole constellation is represented in Fig. 215.

37.text: Ursa Major does not play a conspicuous part among the other constel-

38.text: lations. Six of its stars are supposed to be men shooting with slings, and

39.text: are called accordingly “sling-throwers” (wɪyotkɪñaˊulɪt). The seventh star,

40.text: which is double, is supposed to be a gray fox gnawing at a pair of antlers.
